object_description: three offset elongated pavilion-like school volumes
design_condition: Three offset volumes are placed centrally and subtly raised above the terrain to mediate between the surrounding buildings and railway, while generating varied outdoor spaces around the tree population.

positive.statement: The differentiated volumetrics respond to the specific situation and compose a coherent urban whole.

position.rationale: Offset pavilion masses are clearly visible across the top and elevation projections.

positive.statement: The geometry creates varied opportunities to play and spend time in the outdoor spaces.

position.rationale: Peripheral gaps around the offset volumes indicate distributed outdoor play areas.

positive.statement: The basic levels are functionally well solved, with flexible spaces and useful cloakroom-playroom relationships.

position.rationale: Interior level organization is not exposed, so the marker uses a plausible mid-building surface location.

positive.statement: The reserve multi-purpose room can be used for extracurricular district events and as a reserve classroom.

position.rationale: The reserve room is not distinguishable; placement is constrained to an end pavilion zone.

positive.statement: The project impresses with subtle urban development and good operational use of the school.

position.rationale: Operational assessment applies broadly, anchored to the central sampled building mass.

negative.statement: The relatively large footprint leaves only narrow peripheral areas for children playing outside.

position.target: large footprint and narrow peripheral areas
position.rationale: The elongated footprints visibly consume much of the site, leaving narrow edge strips.

negative.statement: The clearly separated basic levels make collaboration between classes on the same floor difficult.

position.rationale: Class separation is interior; the marker is constrained to an upper-middle pavilion level.

negative.statement: The toilets in the eastern part of the building are too far from the basic level.

position.rationale: The eastern-part constraint places the unseen toilets near the east end of the sampled mass.

negative.statement: The facade is not sufficiently geared toward school use and the pavilion-like expression conflicts with the situation and use.

position.rationale: The pavilion-like exterior and elongated glazed edges are visible on the south-facing perimeter.

negative.statement: The extensive glazing requires glare protection that restricts the optimal use of daylight.

position.rationale: Glazing performance is assigned to the exposed south facade where daylight enters.

negative.statement: Integral elements in the interaction between architecture and technology are missing.

position.rationale: The missing integration is conceptual, anchored to the central building envelope.

negative.statement: The project has poor economic efficiency because of its large outer surface and complex construction.

position.rationale: Economic efficiency is a whole-project judgment without a specific spatial referent.
